points.why: It describes dependence growing as staff left while outsourcing looked safe, but never names Shifting the Burden or explains that the outside fix let in-house skill decay through disuse.
It explains why the city has no alternative now, but not the reinforcing loop in which each year of outsourcing makes rebuilding harder.
It recommends a hybrid that keeps the firm this cycle in a reduced or training role while hiring or training staff and securing a model handover.
It never mentions putting the dependency on a risk register.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly allows keeping the firm this cycle and does not recommend dropping it.
It covers negotiation and competing quotes, but frames the real problem as dependency and recommends rebuilding capability.

notes: It suggests a one-time independent review rather than an internal parallel forecast, which partly but not fully rebuilds the city's own capability.
